reading.title: Reporting accidents, incidents and near misses
paragraphs: 4. REPORTING ACCIDENTS, INCIDENTS AND NEAR MISSES

4.1 The Company's aim is to learn from every event that harms someone, or could have done so. All accidents, cases of work-related ill health and near misses must therefore be reported, however minor they may appear at the time.

4.2 An employee who is injured at work, or who witnesses an accident, must inform his or her line manager straight away and, in any event, before the end of the shift. If first aid is needed, the nearest first aider should be called at once.

4.3 The line manager shall ensure that the area is made safe, enter the details in the accident book and complete an incident report form within 24 hours. The form should record the facts only: what happened, where, when and who was involved. It is not the place to apportion blame.

4.4 A near miss is an event that did not cause injury or damage but could easily have done so. Near misses are a valuable warning. Employees are encouraged to report them using the same form, and may do so anonymously if they prefer.

4.5 The Health and Safety Manager will review each report, decide whether a full investigation is required and notify the enforcing authority where the incident is reportable by law. The findings, together with any corrective action, will be shared with the team concerned.
4.6 No one will suffer any detriment for reporting an incident or raising a safety concern in good faith. Failure to report, on the other hand, may be treated as a disciplinary matter.

options: Within 24 hours
Before the end of the shift at the latest
By the following morning
Once the accident book has been completed
questions.explain_fr: Le texte dit « straight away and, in any event, before the end of the shift ». Les 24 heures concernent le formulaire que remplit le manager.

options: The manager's view of who was responsible
A proposal for disciplinary action
The facts only
The employee's medical details
questions.explain_fr: « The form should record the facts only » et « it is not the place to apportion blame » : on consigne les faits, pas les responsabilités.

options: Because they serve as a warning
Because the law requires every near miss to be notified
Because they are used to assess employees
Because they must be entered in the accident book
questions.explain_fr: « Near misses are a valuable warning » : le presqu'accident d'aujourd'hui annonce l'accident de demain.

questions.q: What may happen to an employee who fails to report an incident?
options: Nothing, since reporting is voluntary
He or she will suffer a detriment
The enforcing authority will be notified
It may be treated as a disciplinary matter
questions.explain_fr: La dernière clause oppose la protection de celui qui signale de bonne foi à la sanction possible de celui qui ne signale pas.

reading.title: Medical unfitness: what the employer must do next
paragraphs: MEMORANDUM - Mr D.: medical unfitness and next steps
You asked what the occupational health physician's opinion of 6 October means for the company, and whether Mr D.'s employment can now be brought to an end. In short: not yet.

Under French law, a finding of unfitness can only be made by the occupational health physician, after examining the employee and studying the position. It is binding on the employer unless it is challenged before the employment tribunal. The opinion does not end the contract; it triggers a duty to look for another role.

The company must therefore carry out a genuine search for a suitable alternative role, taking account of the physician's written findings. The search covers vacant positions in the company and, where it belongs to a group, in the group's other French entities between which staff can be moved. If necessary, the role should be adapted, for instance through adjustments to the workstation or to working hours. The works council must be consulted before any proposal is put to Mr D.

There are two exceptions. No search is required where the physician has expressly stated either that keeping the employee in any job would be seriously detrimental to his health, or that his state of health precludes redeployment to any job. Neither statement appears in the opinion we have received.

Dismissal may be contemplated only if no suitable role exists or if Mr D. turns down the roles offered. Please note that if he has been neither redeployed nor dismissed within one month of the examination, the company must resume paying his salary.
I would suggest that we draw up a list of vacancies this week and keep a written record of every step, since the burden of proving that the search was genuine lies with the employer.

glossary.plain: a formal medical decision that the employee can no longer do the job
having to be followed by
another job that fits the person's skills and medical limits
the body of elected employee representatives
moving someone to a different job in the organisation
refuses

the responsibility for showing that something is true

Yes, because the opinion is binding

options: Only in the site where Mr D. works
In every company of the group worldwide
Only in roles identical to his previous one
In the company and, where relevant, the group's other French entities
questions.explain_fr: Le mémo vise les postes vacants de l'entreprise et, s'il y a un groupe, ceux des autres entités françaises entre lesquelles le personnel peut être permuté.

questions.q: In which case is the employer released from the search?
options: Where the physician expressly states that the employee's health precludes any redeployment
Where the employee has been absent for a long time

Where the company has no time to carry it out

options: His contract ends automatically
The physician must examine him again

reading.title: Friday's stoppage at the Lille warehouse
paragraphs: Subject: Friday's stoppage at the Lille warehouse - where we stand
Hi Brad,

Thanks for your message. I understand why three drivers walking off the job in the middle of a shift looks like insubordination, but under French law it is very likely something else, and I would advise against any disciplinary action for now.

France recognizes what is called the right to withdraw. An employee who has reasonable grounds to believe that a situation presents a serious and imminent danger to their life or health may stop work and step away from it, provided they alert the employer. No prior authorization is needed, and it is not a strike.

The key point is that the test is the employee's reasonable belief, not whether the danger turns out to be real. Here, the drivers reported twice last month that the brakes on two forklifts were unreliable, and one of the trucks failed to stop on the ramp on Friday morning. A court would almost certainly find their belief reasonable.

If that is right, the company can neither discipline them nor dock their pay for the hours not worked. Nor can it ask them to go back until the danger has been dealt with. Doing so could expose the company to serious liability if someone were then hurt.

My suggestion is as follows: take both forklifts out of service today, have them inspected by the supplier, and confirm to the drivers in writing that they will be paid as normal. We should also record the incident and update the risk assessment.
I know this is a long way from how things work in Ohio. I'm happy to walk you through it on a call tomorrow if that would help.
Best regards,
Claire

glossary.plain: stopping work and leaving, usually as a protest
the right to stop work and move away from a serious danger
good, sensible reasons
take money off their wages

glossary.plain: legal responsibility for harm or loss
no longer in use until repaired
explain it to you step by step

legalese.plain: a real danger that could cause harm very soon
on condition that they tell the employer
they do not have to ask for permission first

questions.q: What does Claire advise Brad to do about the three drivers?
options: Give them a written warning
Take no disciplinary action for the moment
Treat the stoppage as a strike
Ask them to return to work at once
questions.explain_fr: « I would advise against any disciplinary action for now » : « to advise against » = déconseiller.

questions.q: What is the legal test for the right to withdraw?
options: Whether the danger was real
Whether the employer had authorised the stoppage
Whether several employees stopped work together
Whether the employee had reasonable grounds to believe there was a serious and imminent danger
questions.explain_fr: Le critère est la croyance raisonnable du salarié, et non la réalité du danger.

questions.q: Why would a court probably side with the drivers?
options: They had already reported the faulty brakes, and a truck failed to stop
They had been with the company for a long time
The forklifts had never been inspected
Their supervisor told them to stop
questions.explain_fr: Deux signalements le mois précédent et un incident le vendredi matin : la croyance au danger était raisonnable.

questions.q: What can the company NOT do if the withdrawal is justified?
options: Have the forklifts inspected
Update the risk assessment
Deduct the hours not worked from the drivers' pay
Confirm matters in writing
questions.explain_fr: « The company can neither discipline them nor dock their pay » : ni sanction ni retenue sur salaire.

reading.title: Work-related stress in Customer Support: findings and recommendations
paragraphs: 3. FINDINGS

3.1 Workload. Two thirds of respondents in the Customer Support team describe their workload as unmanageable at least once a week. Since the reorganisation in March, the team has lost four posts without any reduction in the volume of calls. Several interviewees said that they regularly skip breaks, and absence levels have risen sharply over the same period.

3.2 Control and support. Staff have little say over how their work is scheduled. Team leaders, who are themselves overstretched, admit that one-to-one meetings have largely fallen by the wayside. As a result, early signs of stress tend to go unnoticed until the person is signed off.
3.3 Presenteeism. A number of employees reported coming in ill for fear of adding to their colleagues' burden. This masks the true scale of the problem and delays recovery.
4. RECOMMENDATIONS
4.1 The risks described above should be recorded in the company's risk assessment document without delay, together with a dated action plan.

4.2 As a priority, management should review staffing levels in Customer Support and agree realistic targets with the team. Wellbeing initiatives are welcome, but they are no substitute for tackling the root causes.
4.3 Team leaders should receive training in spotting the signs of burnout and in holding return-to-work interviews. Monthly one-to-one meetings should be reinstated.
4.4 All staff should be reminded of the confidential employee assistance programme and of their right to request an appointment with the occupational health service at any time.
4.5 Progress should be reviewed with the works council's health and safety committee in six months' time.

writing.title: Informing a client of a workplace accident
writing.brief: An accident happened yesterday at your client's Lyon warehouse: a forklift operator injured his foot. Write to Ms Whitfield, the group HR director in London, to tell her what happened, what has been done and what comes next.
writing.brief_fr: Un accident est survenu hier dans l'entrepôt lyonnais de votre client : un cariste s'est blessé au pied. Écrivez à Mme Whitfield, DRH du groupe à Londres, pour l'informer des faits, des mesures prises et de la suite.

gaps.text: I am writing to ___ you of an accident which occurred at the Lyon warehouse yesterday afternoon.
gaps.explain_fr: « To inform someone of something » : la formule d'ouverture classique d'un courrier factuel. Pas de « to » après « inform » : « inform you », jamais « inform to you ».

gaps.text: One of our forklift operators, Mr Karim B., ___ an injury to his left foot when a pallet slipped from the forks.
gaps.explain_fr: « To sustain an injury » est la collocation de l'écrit ; à l'oral on dirait « he hurt his foot ». « To have an injury » est plat, « to get a wound » inexact.

gaps.text: He was ___ first aid on the spot and then taken to hospital as a precaution.
gaps.explain_fr: On « donne » les premiers secours : « to give first aid ». « First aid » est indénombrable, sans article.

gaps.text: The injury is not thought to be serious, although he has been ___ work for ten days.
gaps.explain_fr: « To be signed off (work) » = être arrêté par son médecin (britannique). Ne dites pas « he is stopped » ni « he is arrested ».

gaps.text: The accident was ___ to the health insurance fund this morning, as French law requires.
gaps.explain_fr: « To report an accident to » : déclarer un accident à. « To declare » est réservé à la douane et aux impôts.

gaps.text: We have also opened an investigation in order to ___ exactly what happened.
gaps.explain_fr: « To establish what happened » = établir les faits. Registre soutenu ; « to find out » en est l'équivalent courant.

writing.model:
Subject: Accident at the Lyon warehouse - 14 May

Dear Ms Whitfield,

I am writing to inform you of an accident which occurred at the Lyon warehouse yesterday afternoon.

At around 3.30 pm, one of our forklift operators, Mr Karim B., sustained an injury to his left foot when a pallet slipped from the forks. He was given first aid on the spot and then taken to hospital as a precaution. I am pleased to say that the injury is not thought to be serious, although he has been signed off work for ten days.

The accident was reported to the health insurance fund this morning, as French law requires, and the area has been made safe. We have also opened an investigation in order to establish exactly what happened.

I will send you our findings, together with any corrective action we recommend, by the end of next week.

Please do not hesitate to contact me should you need any further information in the meantime.

Yours sincerely,

Claire Morel
writing.model_us:
Subject: Accident at the Lyon warehouse - May 14

Dear Ms. Whitfield:

I am writing to inform you of an accident that occurred at the Lyon warehouse yesterday afternoon.

At around 3:30 p.m., one of our forklift operators, Mr. Karim B., sustained an injury to his left foot when a pallet slipped from the forks. He was given first aid on the spot and then taken to the hospital as a precaution. I am pleased to say that the injury is not thought to be serious, although he has been put on medical leave for ten days.

The accident was reported to the health insurance fund this morning, as French law requires, and the area has been made safe. We have also opened an investigation to establish exactly what happened.

I will send you our findings, along with any corrective action we recommend, by the end of next week.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you need any further information in the meantime.

Sincerely,

Claire Morel

commentary.quote: I am writing to inform you of an accident
commentary.note_fr: L'objet du message dès la première phrase, sans préambule : c'est ce qu'attend un lecteur britannique pour une mauvaise nouvelle.

commentary.quote: At around 3.30 pm
commentary.note_fr: Les faits dans l'ordre : heure, personne, lésion, circonstances. Notez la ponctuation britannique de l'heure (3.30 pm) ; la version américaine écrit 3:30 p.m.

commentary.quote: I am pleased to say that the injury is not thought to be serious
commentary.note_fr: Le passif « is not thought to be » évite de s'engager sur un pronostic médical : formule prudente et très idiomatique.

commentary.quote: as French law requires
commentary.note_fr: Une incise suffit à signaler au lecteur étranger que la déclaration à la caisse est une obligation, non un choix.

commentary.quote: by the end of next week
commentary.note_fr: Terminez sur un engagement daté : le lecteur sait quand il aura la suite. « By » = au plus tard.

checklist: Does my first sentence say why I am writing?
Have I given the facts in order: when, who, what injury, how?
Have I avoided guessing at causes or blaming anyone?
Have I said what has already been done and what happens next, with a date?
Have I used 'sustained', 'reported' and 'signed off' rather than calques from French?

He sustained an injury to his... when...
He was given first aid on the spot and taken to hospital as a precaution.
The injury is not thought to be serious.
The area has been made safe.
We have opened an investigation in order to establish what happened.
I will send you our findings by...

writing.title: Welcoming an employee back after a long absence
writing.brief: Sophie, a member of your team, is coming back on Monday after three months' sick leave. Write her a warm email proposing a return-to-work meeting and explaining her phased return, without asking anything about her health.
writing.brief_fr: Sophie, membre de votre équipe, reprend lundi après trois mois d'arrêt. Écrivez-lui un e-mail chaleureux pour lui proposer un entretien de retour et lui présenter sa reprise progressive, sans la questionner sur sa santé.

gaps.text: I was very glad to hear that you are feeling ___ and that you will be back with us on Monday 2 June.
gaps.explain_fr: « To feel better » = aller mieux. On évite « you are healed » ou « you are cured », trop médicaux et indiscrets.

gaps.text: The aim is simply to bring you up to ___ on what has changed in the team.
gaps.explain_fr: « To bring someone up to speed » = mettre quelqu'un au courant de ce qu'il a manqué. Expression courante et chaleureuse.

gaps.text: We would like to make your return as ___ as possible.
gaps.explain_fr: « A smooth return » = une reprise en douceur, sans heurts. « Soft » ne convient pas ici.

gaps.text: As recommended by the occupational health physician, you will be on a ___ return for the first four weeks.
gaps.explain_fr: « A phased return » : la reprise progressive. « Progressive » existe mais évoque surtout des idées politiques ou une maladie évolutive.

gaps.text: You do not need to tell me anything about your health that you would ___ keep private.
gaps.explain_fr: « Would rather » + base verbale = préférer. Cette phrase rassure : le manager n'a pas à connaître le diagnostic.

gaps.text: We are all looking forward to ___ you.
gaps.explain_fr: « To look forward to » est suivi du gérondif : « to seeing », jamais « to see ».

writing.model:
Subject: Your return to work on Monday

Dear Sophie,

I was very glad to hear that you are feeling better and that you will be back with us on Monday 2 June.

I would like to suggest that we meet at 10.00 on your first morning for a short return-to-work meeting. There is nothing formal about it. The aim is simply to bring you up to speed on what has changed in the team, and to see how we can make your return as smooth as possible.

As recommended by the occupational health physician, you will be on a phased return for the first four weeks, working mornings only. We can of course review these arrangements at any time if you feel they are not working for you.

You do not need to tell me anything about your health that you would rather keep private. What matters to me is knowing what support you need.

In the meantime, please do not worry about your inbox. Paul has been looking after your files and will hand them back to you gradually.

We are all looking forward to seeing you.

Kind regards,

Nathalie

commentary.quote: I was very glad to hear that you are feeling better
commentary.note_fr: On commence par la personne, pas par l'organisation. « Glad » est plus simple et plus sincère que « delighted » dans ce contexte.

commentary.quote: There is nothing formal about it.
commentary.note_fr: Phrase courte qui désamorce l'inquiétude : après une longue absence, toute convocation peut sembler menaçante.

commentary.quote: We can of course review these arrangements at any time
commentary.note_fr: « Arrangements » = modalités (et non « arrangements » au sens de compromis). « Review » = réexaminer : rien n'est figé.

commentary.quote: What matters to me is knowing what support you need.
commentary.note_fr: Structure emphatique « What matters is... » : elle recentre l'échange sur les besoins, sans toucher au secret médical.

commentary.quote: will hand them back to you gradually
commentary.note_fr: « To hand back » = rendre, restituer. L'adverbe « gradually » prolonge l'idée de reprise progressive jusque dans la charge de travail.

checklist: Does the email open with the person rather than with logistics?
Have I made it clear that the meeting is informal?
Have I explained the phased return and said that it can be reviewed?
Have I avoided any question about the diagnosis?
Is the tone warm without being over-familiar?
phrasebank: I was very glad to hear that you are feeling better.
I would like to suggest that we meet on your first morning.
There is nothing formal about it.
The aim is simply to bring you up to speed.
You will be on a phased return for the first four weeks.
We can review these arrangements at any time.
What matters to me is knowing what support you need.
We are all looking forward to seeing you.

writing.title: Explaining the occupational health physician to a US client
writing.brief: A US client does not understand why an employee returning from four months' sick leave cannot simply come back with a note from her own doctor. Write one paragraph (130-170 words) explaining the role of the médecin du travail and the return-to-work medical examination.
writing.brief_fr: Un client américain ne comprend pas pourquoi une salariée de retour après quatre mois d'arrêt ne peut pas simplement reprendre avec un certificat de son médecin. Rédigez un paragraphe (130 à 170 mots) expliquant le rôle du médecin du travail et la visite de reprise.
outline: Every employer in France must belong to an occupational health service; key figure: the médecin du travail
Contrast with a 'company doctor': independent, preventive role, no treatment, no diagnosis disclosed
What the employer receives: a binding opinion on fitness, with or without adjustments
Consequence after a long absence: a return-to-work medical examination, arranged by the employer
Practical advice: book it as soon as the return date is known
writing.model: In France, every employer must belong to an occupational health service, and the key figure in it is the occupational health physician, known as the médecin du travail. Unlike a company doctor in the American sense, this physician is independent of the employer and has a purely preventive role: he or she does not treat employees, and never tells the company what the diagnosis is. What the company does receive is an opinion on whether the employee is fit for the job, with or without adjustments, and that opinion is binding. This is why, after a long absence, an employee cannot simply resume work on the strength of a note from her own doctor. The employer must first arrange a return-to-work medical examination with the occupational health physician. In practice, I would recommend booking it as soon as you know the return date, since the contract is still regarded as suspended until the examination has taken place.

commentary.quote: the occupational health physician, known as the médecin du travail
commentary.note_fr: L'équivalent anglais d'abord, le terme français ensuite : le client retrouvera ce dernier dans les documents.

commentary.quote: Unlike a company doctor in the American sense
commentary.note_fr: « Unlike » + nom ouvre le contraste avec la référence du lecteur. Plus léger que « contrary to », qui est souvent un calque.

commentary.quote: What the company does receive is
commentary.note_fr: Le « does » d'insistance répond à la phrase précédente (ce que l'entreprise ne reçoit pas). Tournure très naturelle pour rééquilibrer.

commentary.quote: on the strength of a note from her own doctor
commentary.note_fr: « On the strength of » = sur la seule foi de. Expression idiomatique utile pour dire qu'un document ne suffit pas.

commentary.quote: In practice, I would recommend booking it
commentary.note_fr: « To recommend » + gérondif (ou « that you book »), jamais « recommend you to book ». « In practice » annonce le conseil concret.

checklist: Have I given an English equivalent before the French term?
Have I drawn the contrast with what my reader knows (the company doctor)?
Is it clear who arranges the examination and why it matters?
Does the paragraph end with a practical recommendation?
Have I linked my sentences without overusing 'moreover' or 'indeed'?
phrasebank: The key figure is..., known as...
Unlike..., this physician is independent of the employer.
What the company does receive is an opinion on...
This is why an employee cannot simply...
The employer must first arrange...
In practice, I would recommend...

writing.title: Minuting a near miss at the health and safety committee
writing.brief: You are taking the minutes of the health and safety committee. Write the item (120-160 words) on a near miss in the loading bay: the facts, the initial findings, the employee representative's remark and the actions agreed.
writing.brief_fr: Vous rédigez le compte rendu de la commission santé et sécurité. Rédigez le point (120 à 160 mots) consacré à un presqu'accident sur le quai de chargement : faits, premiers constats, remarque du représentant du personnel et actions décidées.
outline: Facts: 12 September, a pallet fell from a forklift, one metre from a delivery driver, nobody injured
Initial findings: load not secured; pedestrians and vehicles share the same route
Remark by Mr Lambert (employee representative): similar incident raised in June, no follow-up
Chair's response
Actions agreed, with deadlines and the person responsible
writing.model:
3. Near miss in the loading bay (12 September)

The Health and Safety Manager reported that a pallet had fallen from a forklift truck in the loading bay, landing roughly one metre from a delivery driver. Nobody was injured. The initial investigation points to two contributing factors: the load had not been properly secured, and pedestrians and vehicles share the same route at that point. Mr Lambert, for the employee representatives, noted that a similar incident had been raised in June without any follow-up. The Chair acknowledged this and apologised for the delay. It was agreed that (a) a marked pedestrian walkway would be installed by 15 October; (b) all forklift operators would attend refresher training before the end of the month; and (c) the risk assessment would be updated accordingly.

Action: Health and Safety Manager. Progress to be reviewed at the next meeting.

commentary.quote: reported that a pallet had fallen
commentary.note_fr: Le compte rendu est au discours indirect et au passé : « reported that... had fallen ». Pas de présent de narration.

commentary.quote: The initial investigation points to two contributing factors
commentary.note_fr: « Points to » reste prudent (l'enquête n'est pas terminée) ; « contributing factors » évite de désigner un coupable.

commentary.quote: noted that a similar incident had been raised in June without any follow-up
commentary.note_fr: « Noted » est le verbe neutre du rédacteur : il consigne la critique sans la dramatiser ni l'édulcorer.

commentary.quote: It was agreed that
commentary.note_fr: La formule consacrée pour les décisions. Suivent des propositions parallèles (a), (b), (c), chacune avec « would » et une échéance.

commentary.quote: Progress to be reviewed at the next meeting.
commentary.note_fr: Style télégraphique admis en fin de point : « to be reviewed » = à réexaminer.

checklist: Is everything in the past tense and in reported speech?
Have I separated facts, findings, discussion and decisions?
Is every action given a deadline and an owner?
Have I recorded the criticism neutrally?
Would someone who was not at the meeting understand what was decided?
phrasebank: The Health and Safety Manager reported that...
Nobody was injured.
The initial investigation points to...
Mr X, for the employee representatives, noted that...
The Chair acknowledged this and...
It was agreed that...
Action: ... Progress to be reviewed at the next meeting.

writing.title: Offering an alternative role after a finding of unfitness
writing.brief: Mr Dubois, a warehouse operative, has been declared unfit for his position. Write the letter (200-250 words) offering him the position of Stock Control Administrator: recall the physician's findings, the search carried out, the features of the role and the deadline for his answer.
writing.brief_fr: M. Dubois, magasinier, a été déclaré inapte à son poste. Rédigez la lettre (200 à 250 mots) lui proposant le poste de gestionnaire de stocks : rappel des conclusions du médecin du travail, recherche effectuée, caractéristiques du poste et délai de réponse.
outline: Heading and reminder of the finding of unfitness and of the physician's written findings
The search carried out and the consultation of the works council
The offer: job title, site, duties, hours, pay
Training and confirmation that the role is compatible with the physician's recommendations
Deadline for a written answer; offer to discuss or to visit the workstation
writing.model:
Dear Mr Dubois,

Proposal of an alternative position following the finding of medical unfitness

Following your examination on 6 October, the occupational health physician declared you unfit for your position as warehouse operative. In his written findings, he indicated that you could hold a sedentary position involving no carrying of loads.

In accordance with our duty to seek redeployment, we have carried out a search for suitable positions within the company and the other French entities of the group. The works council was consulted on the outcome of that search on 20 October.

We are now able to offer you the position of Stock Control Administrator at our Lyon site. The main features of this position are as follows:

- duties: monitoring stock levels and preparing order documents, as described in the attached job description;
- working hours: 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday;
- remuneration: unchanged.

Training in the stock management software would be provided during your first month. The occupational health physician has confirmed that this position is compatible with his recommendations.

We would be grateful if you could let us know in writing by 7 November whether you accept this proposal. Should you wish to discuss it or to visit the workstation beforehand, please contact me directly.

Yours sincerely,

Claire Morel
Human Resources Manager

commentary.quote: declared you unfit for your position as warehouse operative
commentary.note_fr: « Unfit for your position » : l'inaptitude vise le poste, non la personne. Évitez « incapable » ou « unable », qui sonnent comme un jugement.

commentary.quote: In accordance with our duty to seek redeployment
commentary.note_fr: « In accordance with » introduit le fondement de la démarche. La lettre servira de preuve : elle doit montrer que la recherche a été faite.

commentary.quote: We are now able to offer you the position of
commentary.note_fr: « We are now able to » : plus chaleureux que « we hereby propose ». Notez « to offer someone a position », sans préposition.

commentary.quote: The main features of this position are as follows:
commentary.note_fr: « As follows » suivi de deux points annonce une liste. Jamais « as following » ni « are the followings ».

commentary.quote: We would be grateful if you could let us know in writing by 7 November
commentary.note_fr: Demande polie + forme de la réponse + échéance (« by » = au plus tard le) : les trois éléments tiennent en une phrase.

commentary.quote: Should you wish to discuss it or to visit the workstation beforehand
commentary.note_fr: Inversion « Should you wish » = « If you wish », registre soutenu. « Beforehand » = au préalable.

checklist: Have I recalled the physician's findings accurately and neutrally?
Does the letter show that a genuine search was carried out and that the works council was consulted?
Is the role described precisely enough for the employee to decide?
Have I given a clear deadline and said how to reply?
Is the tone respectful, with no suggestion that the employee is at fault?
phrasebank: Following your examination on..., the occupational health physician declared you unfit for your position as...
In accordance with our duty to seek redeployment, we have carried out a search for...
The works council was consulted on...
We are now able to offer you the position of...
The main features of this position are as follows:
This position is compatible with the physician's recommendations.
We would be grateful if you could let us know in writing by...
Should you wish to discuss it, please contact me directly.

writing.title: Reporting on a labour inspector's visit
writing.brief: The labour inspector made an unannounced visit to your client's Nantes site yesterday. Write to David, the group's health and safety director in Manchester (200-250 words): how the visit went, the three points raised, what to expect next and your proposed action plan.
writing.brief_fr: L'inspectrice du travail a effectué hier un contrôle inopiné sur le site nantais de votre client. Écrivez à David, directeur santé-sécurité du groupe à Manchester (200 à 250 mots) : déroulement de la visite, les trois points relevés, la suite prévisible et votre plan d'action.
outline: Purpose of the email
How the visit went: length, what the inspector looked at, atmosphere
The three points raised (risk assessment not updated, hearing protection, press guard)
What the inspector said would happen next
Action already taken and proposed action plan
Next step and offer of a call
writing.model:
Subject: Labour inspectorate visit, Nantes site - summary and action plan

Dear David,

As promised, here is a summary of yesterday's unannounced inspection of the Nantes site.

The labour inspector spent around three hours on site. She toured the workshop, spoke to several operators and asked to see the risk assessment document, the accident records and the training files. The visit was courteous and the site manager cooperated fully.

Three points were raised. First, the risk assessment document has not been updated since the new packaging line was installed. Second, two operators were not wearing hearing protection in a designated noise area. Third, the guard on one of the presses had been removed.

The inspector told us that she would confirm her observations in writing and that we should expect a formal notice to comply in respect of the press. No penalty has been mentioned at this stage.

We have already taken the press out of service. In addition, I would suggest the following:

- update the risk assessment by the end of the month, with the works council's involvement;
- hold a toolbox talk on hearing protection this week;
- review machine guarding across the site.

I will forward the inspector's letter as soon as it arrives. In the meantime, I would be happy to go through any of this on a call.

Kind regards,

Claire

commentary.quote: As promised, here is a summary of yesterday's unannounced inspection
commentary.note_fr: Entrée en matière directe. « Unannounced inspection » et non « control » : « to control » ne veut pas dire vérifier.

commentary.quote: Three points were raised. First,
commentary.note_fr: On annonce le nombre, puis « First / Second / Third » : le lecteur pressé repère immédiatement la structure. Le passif évite de répéter « the inspector ».

commentary.quote: we should expect a formal notice to comply in respect of the press
commentary.note_fr: « Formal notice to comply » rend la mise en demeure sans recourir à un terme britannique qui aurait un sens technique différent. « In respect of » = concernant (soutenu).

commentary.quote: No penalty has been mentioned at this stage.
commentary.note_fr: « At this stage » : précision honnête, qui rassure sans rien promettre.

commentary.quote: In addition, I would suggest the following:
commentary.note_fr: « I would suggest » adoucit la recommandation ; la liste à puces à l'infinitif rend le plan d'action lisible d'un coup d'œil.

commentary.quote: I would be happy to go through any of this on a call
commentary.note_fr: « To go through » = passer en revue. Clôture naturelle entre collègues, moins raide que « do not hesitate to contact me ».

checklist: Can the reader tell within two lines what happened and how serious it is?
Are the inspector's three points stated factually, without excuses?
Have I distinguished what has been done from what I propose?
Does each action have a deadline or a time frame?
Have I avoided 'control' for 'inspection' and untranslated French acronyms?
phrasebank: As promised, here is a summary of...
The inspector asked to see...
Three points were raised. First, ... Second, ... Third, ...
We should expect a formal notice to comply in respect of...
No penalty has been mentioned at this stage.
We have already taken... out of service.
In addition, I would suggest the following:
I would be happy to go through any of this on a call.

dialogues.title: First morning back
dialogues.context: Helen, an HR manager in Leeds, holds a return-to-work meeting with Raj, an account manager who has been signed off for six weeks with stress.
dialogues.context_fr: Helen, responsable RH à Leeds, reçoit en entretien de retour Raj, chargé de clientèle, arrêté six semaines pour stress.

lines.speaker: Helen
lines.text: Morning, Raj. It's really good to have you back. Grab a seat. How are you feeling?
lines.note_fr: « It's good to have you back » : la formule d'accueil attendue. « Grab a seat » = asseyez-vous (familier et chaleureux).

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Not too bad, thanks. A bit nervous, to be honest. Six weeks is a long time.
lines.note_fr: « Not too bad » : litote britannique, qui signifie plutôt « ça va bien ».

lines.speaker: Helen
lines.text: That's completely understandable. Just so you know, this isn't anything formal. I only want to make sure we get your return right.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: I appreciate that. My GP's suggested a phased return, mornings only for the first fortnight.
lines.note_fr: « GP » (general practitioner) = médecin traitant. « A fortnight » = quinze jours, mot strictement britannique.

lines.speaker: Helen
lines.text: Yes, I've seen the fit note, and that's absolutely fine with us. We'll build your hours back up gradually and see how it goes.
lines.note_fr: « To build up one's hours » = augmenter progressivement son temps de travail.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Thanks. What worries me most is the workload. Before I went off, I was covering two portfolios.
lines.note_fr: « To go off (sick) » = partir en arrêt. « To cover » = assurer l'intérim de.

lines.speaker: Helen
lines.text: I know, and that shouldn't have gone on for as long as it did. Tom has taken over the Northern accounts for good, so you'll only have your own.
lines.note_fr: « For good » = définitivement. Notez l'aveu mesuré : « that shouldn't have gone on for as long as it did ».

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: That's a relief. And the Friday reporting?

lines.speaker: Helen
lines.text: We've moved it to Monday so nobody's working late at the end of the week. Is there anything else that would make things easier?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Maybe a quick catch-up with you every week or so, just at the beginning?
lines.note_fr: « A catch-up » = un point rapide. « Every week or so » = toutes les semaines environ.

lines.speaker: Helen
lines.text: Of course. Let's say Thursdays at ten. And if things start to pile up before then, don't wait. Come and find me.
lines.note_fr: « To pile up » = s'accumuler. « Don't wait » invite à signaler tôt les difficultés.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: I will. Thanks, Helen. That's a weight off my mind.
lines.note_fr: « A weight off my mind » = un poids en moins.

questions.q: What has Raj's doctor recommended?
options: Two more weeks off work
A phased return, working mornings only at first
A permanent move to part-time work
A change of job
questions.explain_fr: « A phased return, mornings only for the first fortnight » : reprise progressive, le matin seulement pendant quinze jours.

questions.q: What has changed in Raj's workload?
options: He now covers two portfolios
He no longer has any reporting to do
Tom has permanently taken over the Northern accounts
His accounts have been given to Helen
questions.explain_fr: « Tom has taken over the Northern accounts for good » : Raj ne garde que son propre portefeuille.

questions.q: What does Helen ask Raj to do if work starts to pile up?
options: Come and tell her without waiting
Raise it at the Thursday meeting
Speak to his GP
Put it in writing
questions.explain_fr: « Don't wait. Come and find me. » : elle l'invite à venir la voir sans attendre le point hebdomadaire.

dialogues.title: A near miss on the loading bay
dialogues.context: Claire, a French HR consultant, is on a call with Graham, UK operations director of a logistics group, the morning after a near miss at the group's French warehouse.
dialogues.context_fr: Claire, consultante RH française, s'entretient par téléphone avec Graham, directeur des opérations britannique d'un groupe de logistique, au lendemain d'un presqu'accident dans l'entrepôt français du groupe.

lines.speaker: Graham
lines.text: Morning, Claire. I gather we had a bit of a scare in Orléans yesterday.
lines.note_fr: « I gather » = j'ai cru comprendre. « A bit of a scare » : euphémisme typiquement britannique pour une grosse frayeur.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: We did. A pallet came off a forklift and landed about a metre from a delivery driver. Nobody was hurt, thankfully.

lines.speaker: Graham
lines.text: Well, that's the main thing. So, strictly speaking, it's a near miss rather than an accident. Do we need to report it to anyone?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Not to the authorities, no, since nobody was injured. But I'd strongly recommend we treat it exactly as we would an accident internally.
lines.note_fr: « I'd strongly recommend (that) we treat » : subjonctif sans « should », courant après « recommend ».

lines.speaker: Graham
lines.text: Meaning a full investigation? It seems rather a lot for something that didn't actually happen.
lines.note_fr: « Rather a lot » : litote. Graham trouve la démarche franchement excessive.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I see your point, but it very nearly did happen. And apparently a similar incident was flagged in June and nothing came of it.
lines.note_fr: « I see your point, but » : on accueille l'objection avant de la contrer. « Nothing came of it » = cela n'a rien donné.

lines.speaker: Graham
lines.text: Ah. That does change things.
lines.note_fr: « That does change things » : le « does » d'insistance marque que Graham révise sa position.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: It does. In France the employer has to show it took the necessary preventive measures. If someone's hurt next time and we knew about the risk, we're in a very weak position.

lines.speaker: Graham
lines.text: Fair enough. What do you need from me?
lines.note_fr: « Fair enough » = d'accord, c'est entendu : on se range à l'argument.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Two things, really. A budget for a marked pedestrian walkway, and your backing for refresher training for all the forklift operators.

lines.speaker: Graham
lines.text: You've got both. Can you put it on the agenda for the next safety committee as well?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: It's already on there. And I'll make sure the risk assessment is updated before the end of the month.

questions.q: Why does the incident not have to be reported to the authorities?
options: Because it happened in France
Because the driver was not an employee
Because nobody was injured
Because Graham decided against it
questions.explain_fr: « Not to the authorities, no, since nobody was injured » : sans lésion, pas de déclaration d'accident du travail.

questions.q: What makes Graham change his mind about an investigation?
options: The cost of a pedestrian walkway
The driver's complaint
A request from the safety committee
The fact that a similar incident had been flagged in June
questions.explain_fr: « That does change things » répond à l'information sur l'incident de juin resté sans suite.

questions.q: What does Claire ask Graham for?
options: A budget for a walkway and support for refresher training
A new forklift and a new supplier
A written report for the labour inspector
Permission to update the risk assessment
questions.explain_fr: « Two things, really » : un budget pour une allée piétonne balisée et son appui pour une formation de recyclage.

dialogues.title: Do we file a workers' comp claim?
dialogues.context: Dana, HR director of a US company in Chicago, calls Claire, a French HR consultant, after an employee of the Paris office fell on the stairs and broke her wrist.
dialogues.context_fr: Dana, DRH d'une société américaine à Chicago, appelle Claire, consultante RH française, après la chute dans l'escalier d'une salariée du bureau de Paris, qui s'est cassé le poignet.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: Hi Claire. So I just heard about Emma's fall. Is she okay?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: She's fine, all things considered. A broken wrist, so she'll be out for about a month.
lines.note_fr: « All things considered » = tout bien considéré. « To be out » (US) = être absent, en arrêt.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: Poor thing. Okay, so walk me through the process. Over here I'd file a workers' comp claim with our carrier. What's the equivalent?
lines.note_fr: « Walk me through » = expliquez-moi étape par étape. « Carrier » (US) = compagnie d'assurance.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: It's a little different. There's no private carrier. Workplace accidents are covered by social security, and it's the employer who has to report the accident to the health insurance fund.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: Got it. And how long do we have?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Forty-eight hours from the moment we knew about it. It happened yesterday afternoon, so I filed the report this morning.
lines.note_fr: Le délai de quarante-huit heures court à compter du moment où l'employeur a connaissance de l'accident.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: That was fast. Now, between us, she was on her phone when she fell. Does that make a difference?
lines.note_fr: « Between us » = entre nous. « To be on one's phone » = être en train d'utiliser son téléphone.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Not really. If it happens at work, during working hours, it's presumed to be work-related. We can add a comment to the report if we have serious doubts, but honestly, I wouldn't here.
lines.note_fr: « It's presumed to be work-related » : la présomption d'imputabilité. « I wouldn't here » : conseil net, sans brutalité.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: Okay. And can she sue us on top of that?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Only in one situation: if she could show we knew about a danger and did nothing. It's called inexcusable fault. Was there anything wrong with the stairs?
lines.note_fr: « Faute inexcusable » : Claire en donne la définition avant le nom, ce qui est plus clair pour un non-juriste.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: Not that I know of. But let's get facilities to check the handrail and the lighting anyway.
lines.note_fr: « Not that I know of » = pas à ma connaissance. « Facilities » (US) = les services généraux.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Good idea. I'll put that in writing so it's on file.
lines.note_fr: « On file » = au dossier, consigné.

questions.q: Who has to report a workplace accident in France?
options: The employer, to the health insurance fund
The employee, to a private insurer
The doctor, to the labour inspector
The insurance carrier, to the employer
questions.explain_fr: « It's the employer who has to report the accident to the health insurance fund » : la déclaration incombe à l'employeur.

questions.q: Does it matter that Emma was on her phone when she fell?
options: Yes, the accident is no longer work-related
Yes, she will lose her benefits
No, an accident at work during working hours is presumed to be work-related
No, because nobody saw her
questions.explain_fr: L'accident survenu au temps et au lieu du travail est présumé professionnel.

questions.q: When could Emma take action against the company?
options: Whenever she is injured at work
Never, as in the United States
Only if the company fails to report the accident
If the company knew about a danger and did nothing
questions.explain_fr: C'est la faute inexcusable : l'employeur avait ou aurait dû avoir conscience du danger et n'a pas pris les mesures nécessaires.

dialogues.title: A wellness app won't fix it
dialogues.context: Mark, a US vice president of sales, talks to Claire, a French HR consultant, about the Paris sales team: two people are out with burnout and a third has just resigned.
dialogues.context_fr: Mark, vice-président des ventes américain, échange avec Claire, consultante RH française, au sujet de l'équipe commerciale de Paris : deux personnes sont en arrêt pour burn-out et une troisième vient de démissionner.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Claire, I'll be straight with you. I've got a quarter to close, and half the Paris team is out. What's going on over there?
lines.note_fr: « I'll be straight with you » = je vais être franc. Style direct, typiquement américain.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I'll be just as straight. Two people are out with burnout, and from what I'm hearing, more are close to it.
lines.note_fr: « To be out with burnout » (US) ; un Britannique dirait « off with burnout ».

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Look, everybody's stressed. It's sales. We rolled out that wellness app last year. Aren't they using it?
lines.note_fr: « To roll out » = déployer. « Look, » en tête de phrase annonce une objection.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Some are. But an app doesn't change the fact that the targets went up thirty percent while the team lost two people.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: So what are you telling me? That I need to lower the targets?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I'm telling you that you have a legal problem as well as a people problem. In France, the employer's safety duty covers mental health, and workload is part of that.
lines.note_fr: « A legal problem as well as a people problem » : parallélisme efficace pour faire passer le message.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Meaning what, in practice?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Meaning that if someone burns out and can show the company knew about the overload and did nothing, you're exposed. And right now it's all in writing. They've been raising it in emails since March.
lines.note_fr: « You're exposed » = vous êtes en risque (juridiquement). « To raise » = signaler, soulever.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. That I didn't know. What do you need from me?
lines.note_fr: « That I didn't know » : inversion expressive à l'oral, pour insister sur « that ».

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Three things. Backfill the two open positions, revisit the Q3 targets with the team, and let me run a proper stress risk assessment.
lines.note_fr: « To backfill a position » (US) = pourvoir un poste laissé vacant.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: The first two I can sell upstairs. How long would the assessment take?
lines.note_fr: « To sell something upstairs » = le faire accepter par la direction.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: About three weeks. And I'd rather we did it before the labor inspector asks why we haven't.
lines.note_fr: « I'd rather we did » : prétérit après « would rather » quand le sujet change.

questions.q: According to Claire, why has the wellness app not solved the problem?
options: Nobody is using it
It was rolled out too late
It does nothing about higher targets and a smaller team
It is not available in French
questions.explain_fr: L'application ne change rien à la cause : des objectifs en hausse de trente pour cent avec deux personnes de moins.

questions.q: Why does Claire say Mark has a legal problem?
options: Because the employer's safety duty in France covers mental health and workload
Because the app breaches data protection rules
Because an employee has resigned
Because the targets were not put in writing
questions.explain_fr: L'obligation de sécurité de l'employeur s'étend à la santé mentale, donc à la charge de travail.

questions.q: What does Mark agree he can get approved?
options: The stress risk assessment only
Filling the two open positions and revisiting the targets
Lowering the targets by thirty percent
A meeting with the labor inspector
questions.explain_fr: « The first two I can sell upstairs » : les recrutements de remplacement et la révision des objectifs.

roleplays.title: Explaining unfitness and redeployment to a UK HR director
roleplays.situation: You are advising Fiona, HR director of a British group. A machine operator at the French subsidiary has just been declared unfit for his position by the occupational health physician. Fiona wants to know what this means and how quickly the matter can be closed.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous conseillez Fiona, DRH d'un groupe britannique. Un conducteur de machine de la filiale française vient d'être déclaré inapte à son poste par le médecin du travail. Fiona veut savoir ce que cela implique et en combien de temps le dossier peut être réglé.

turns.say: So the doctor says he's unfit. In the UK we'd get an occupational health report and then take our own view. Can't we do the same?
turns.model: I'm afraid not. In France the occupational health physician's opinion is binding on the employer, not just advisory. We can challenge it before the employment tribunal, but we can't simply set it aside and take our own view.
turns.tips_fr: Commencez par un refus poli (« I'm afraid not ») puis opposez « binding » à « advisory » : c'est le contraste que comprend un interlocuteur britannique.

turns.say: Right. So if he can't do the job, presumably we can dismiss him on capability grounds?
turns.model: Not straight away. The finding of unfitness triggers a duty to look for another role for him, in the company and in the group's other French entities. Dismissal only becomes possible if there's genuinely nothing suitable, or if he turns down what we offer.
turns.tips_fr: « Not straight away » nuance sans contredire. « To trigger a duty » = déclencher une obligation ; « to turn down » = refuser.

turns.say: And how thorough does that search have to be? We're hardly going to invent a job for him.
turns.model: You don't have to create a job, but the search has to be genuine and you have to be able to prove it. That means looking at real vacancies, considering adjustments or training, and consulting the works council. I'd keep a written record of every step.
turns.tips_fr: Rassurez d'abord (« you don't have to create a job »), puis posez l'exigence. « Genuine » = réel, sérieux ; faux ami de « génial ».

turns.say: Fine. And what's the timescale? I'd rather this didn't drag on for months.
turns.model: It shouldn't. There's a practical deadline: if he's neither redeployed nor dismissed within a month of the medical examination, you have to start paying his salary again, even though he isn't working. So it's in everyone's interest to move quickly, but properly.
turns.tips_fr: Donnez le délai et sa conséquence concrète. « To drag on » = traîner en longueur ; terminez sur une formule équilibrée : « quickly, but properly ».

turns.say: Understood. What would you like me to do first?
turns.model: Could you ask the French entities for a list of their current vacancies by Friday? In the meantime, I'll go back to the physician to check exactly what kind of work he could still do. Once we have both, we can see what we're able to offer him.
turns.tips_fr: Une demande précise, datée, puis ce que vous faites de votre côté : « in the meantime, I'll... ». « To go back to someone » = revenir vers quelqu'un.

roleplays.title: A return-to-work conversation
roleplays.situation: You are the HR manager. Marc, a project manager, is back today after ten weeks' sick leave. You do not know the medical reason and must not ask. Welcome him, explain the arrangements and find out what support he needs.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous êtes responsable RH. Marc, chef de projet, reprend aujourd'hui après dix semaines d'arrêt. Vous ignorez le motif médical et ne devez pas le demander. Accueillez-le, expliquez-lui les modalités de reprise et identifiez ses besoins.

turns.say: Morning. Well, here I am. It feels a bit strange to be back, I must say.
turns.model: It's really good to see you, Marc. I can imagine it feels strange after ten weeks, and that's perfectly normal. There's no pressure today. I just want us to have a chat about how to make your return as smooth as possible.
turns.tips_fr: Accueillez la personne avant de parler d'organisation. « There's no pressure » et « have a chat » installent un ton informel.

turns.say: Thanks. I suppose you want to know what was wrong with me.
turns.model: Not at all. That's entirely your business, and you don't have to tell me anything you'd rather keep private. What I do need to know is whether there's anything we can do to make work easier for you.
turns.tips_fr: Ne posez aucune question sur le diagnostic. « That's entirely your business » puis recentrez sur les besoins avec le « do » d'insistance.

turns.say: Well, the doctor mentioned something about not going back full-time straight away.
turns.model: Yes, and we're very happy to follow that. The idea is a phased return: mornings only for the first three weeks, and then we build your hours back up. You'll also see the occupational health physician on Thursday, and we'll adapt the plan to whatever she recommends.
turns.tips_fr: « A phased return », « to build your hours back up » : le vocabulaire de la reprise progressive. Mentionnez la visite de reprise sans jargon.

turns.say: And what about the Delta project? I left it in a real mess.
turns.model: Please don't worry about that. Julie has been running it while you were away, and it's in good shape. I'd suggest she keeps the lead for now and hands things back to you bit by bit, once you feel ready.
turns.tips_fr: Rassurez sans minimiser. « In good shape » = en bon état ; « bit by bit » = petit à petit ; « for now » laisse la porte ouverte.

turns.say: That sounds sensible. And if I find it's too much?
turns.model: Then tell me straight away, and we'll adjust. Nothing here is set in stone. Shall we put a short catch-up in the diary every Friday for the first month, just to see how things are going?
turns.tips_fr: « Nothing is set in stone » = rien n'est figé. Concluez par une proposition concrète avec « Shall we... ? ».

roleplays.title: Debriefing a US plant manager after a labour inspector's visit
roleplays.situation: You are an HR consultant. Steve, the American manager of a plant in France, has just had an unannounced visit from the labour inspector, who found a machine with its guard removed and an out-of-date risk assessment. Steve is irritated. Explain what the inspector can do and what needs to happen now.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous êtes consultant(e) RH. Steve, directeur américain d'une usine en France, vient de recevoir la visite inopinée de l'inspectrice du travail, qui a relevé une machine sans carter de protection et un document unique non mis à jour. Steve est agacé. Expliquez-lui les pouvoirs de l'inspection et la marche à suivre.

turns.say: She just showed up, no appointment, no warrant, and walked right onto my shop floor. Is she even allowed to do that?
turns.model: She is, I'm afraid. In France a labor inspector can enter any workplace at any time without notice, and she can talk to anyone on site. Getting in her way is actually a criminal offense, so cooperating was absolutely the right call.
turns.tips_fr: Réponse nette puis explication. « Without notice » = sans préavis. Valorisez sa réaction : « the right call » = la bonne décision.

turns.say: Okay. So what happens now? Back home OSHA would send me a citation and a fine.
turns.model: It works a little differently here. She'll usually write to you first with her observations, and for the press she'll probably give you formal notice to fix it by a certain date. If it isn't fixed, she can then report the offense to the prosecutor.
turns.tips_fr: Reprenez sa référence (OSHA, citation) pour marquer la différence. « Formal notice to fix it » rend la mise en demeure simplement.

turns.say: And this risk assessment document she kept asking about. Is that really such a big deal?
turns.model: It is. Every employer in France has to keep a written risk assessment and update it whenever something significant changes, like your new packaging line. It's the first thing an inspector asks for, and if there's ever an accident, it's the first thing a court will look at.
turns.tips_fr: « It is. » : réponse courte qui reprend l'auxiliaire. Donnez un exemple tiré de sa propre usine pour rendre la règle concrète.

turns.say: All right, I hear you. What do I need to do this week?
turns.model: Three things. First, keep that press out of service until the guard is back on. Second, let's update the risk assessment together and involve the works council. And third, I'd reply to the inspector in writing as soon as her letter arrives, setting out what you've already done.
turns.tips_fr: Structurez avec « First / Second / And third ». « Out of service » = à l'arrêt ; « setting out » = en exposant.

turns.say: Fine. Could I be personally on the hook for any of this?
turns.model: Potentially, yes. In France the head of a site can be held personally liable for safety offenses, which is why this deserves your attention. The best protection is to show that you acted quickly and that everything is documented.
turns.tips_fr: Soyez honnête sans dramatiser : « Potentially, yes. » « To be on the hook » (familier) est repris par « to be held personally liable » (juridique).

roleplays.title: Persuading a sceptical manager to assess stress risks
roleplays.situation: You are an HR consultant. Olivia, managing director of the French subsidiary of a British group, thinks that including work-related stress in the risk assessment is a box-ticking exercise. Persuade her that it is both a legal requirement and good management.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous êtes consultant(e) RH. Olivia, directrice générale de la filiale française d'un groupe britannique, estime qu'intégrer le stress au travail dans l'évaluation des risques relève de la pure formalité. Convainquez-la que c'est à la fois une obligation légale et un acte de bonne gestion.

turns.say: We're an office, not a building site. I really don't see what risks there are to assess.
turns.model: I take your point: nobody's going to fall off a scaffold here. But in France the risk assessment has to cover mental health as well as physical safety. In an office, the main risks are precisely things like workload, pressure and the way change is handled.
turns.tips_fr: « I take your point » accueille l'objection ; l'image de l'échafaudage montre que vous l'avez comprise avant de la dépasser.

turns.say: People are under pressure everywhere. That's just working life, isn't it?
turns.model: Some pressure is normal, of course, and even healthy. The question is whether it's becoming harmful. Your absence levels in the finance team have doubled since January, and two people have been signed off. To me, that suggests it's worth a closer look.
turns.tips_fr: Concédez puis distinguez « pressure » et « harmful ». Appuyez-vous sur des faits chiffrés et concluez par une litote : « worth a closer look ».

turns.say: And what would this involve? I don't want consultants interviewing my staff for months.
turns.model: It needn't be heavy at all. I'd suggest a short anonymous survey, a handful of group discussions and a meeting with the employee representatives. Three weeks at most. You'd end up with a clear picture and a short action plan to add to the risk assessment document.
turns.tips_fr: « It needn't be » (UK) = ce n'est pas forcément. Décrivez une démarche brève et bornée : « three weeks at most ».

turns.say: Supposing I say no. What's the worst that could happen?
turns.model: Frankly, if someone burned out and brought a claim, the first question would be what the company had done to prevent it. With nothing in writing, you'd find that very hard to answer. And the labour inspector could ask for the document at any time.
turns.tips_fr: « Frankly » annonce une réponse directe ; les conditionnels (« if someone burned out... would be ») maintiennent le ton hypothétique, sans menace.

functional.function: Asking after someone's health without prying
functional.function_fr: Prendre des nouvelles de la santé de quelqu'un sans être indiscret

phrases.text: How are you feeling today?
It's really good to have you back.
I hope you are now fully recovered.
You don't have to tell me anything you'd rather keep private.
Is there anything we can do to make things easier for you?
How are you finding it, being back?
How are you holding up?
Please let me know if there is any support you need at any stage.

functional.function: Reporting an incident and raising a safety concern
functional.function_fr: Signaler un incident et faire part d'une inquiétude pour la sécurité

phrases.text: I'd like to report an incident that happened this morning.
I wish to raise a concern regarding the condition of the equipment.
I'm not comfortable with the way those pallets are stacked.
Somebody is going to get hurt if we leave it like that.
We had a near miss on the loading bay earlier.
We had a close call on the loading dock earlier.
Can I flag something before we start?
For the record, this is the second time the issue has been reported.

functional.function_fr: Proposer des aménagements et offrir son soutien

phrases.text: What would make the biggest difference to you day to day?
We could look at reducing your hours for the first few weeks.
Would it help if you worked from home a couple of days a week?
The Company is prepared to consider any reasonable adjustment to your workstation.
The Company is prepared to consider any reasonable accommodation you may need.
Let's try it for a month and see how it goes.
Nothing is set in stone. We can always revisit it.
Just say the word if it gets too much.
